thread.title: Netflix earnings send stock surging, suggest huge decline was ‘an aberration’ - MarketWatch

author: Sarah Toy
title: Netflix earnings send stock surging, suggest huge decline was ‘an aberration’ - MarketWatch
text:
Investors wasted no time after Netflix Inc. NFLX, +3.98% announced it beat third-quarter earnings expectations Tuesday afternoon, sending shares of the streaming giant up 11% in after-hours trading.
Netflix reported adding a net 6.96 million subscribers in the most recent quarter, with 1.09 million coming from the U.S. and 5.87 million coming from overseas, soundly beating the FactSet consensus of 5.32 million and the company’s own forecast of 5 million. Netflix missed subscriber growth expectations last quarter, which sent the stock into a nosedive .
“One of the big questions after they missed the earnings and membership numbers in Q2 was whether it was just an aberration or a sign of weakening business,” Forrester principal analyst Jim Nail said. “These numbers show that it was clearly an aberration.”
See Also Trump Suggests 'Rogue Killers' Could Be Behind Missing Journalist × Net income for the third quarter rose to $403 million, or 89 cents a share, from $129.6 million, or 29 cents a share, in the same quarter a year ago. The FactSet consensus for the third quarter was 68 cents a share. Revenue rose to $4 billion, beating the FactSet consensus of $3.99 billion and up 25% from $2.99 billion a year ago.
Netflix forecast sunny days ahead for the fourth quarter, saying it expects total net additions of 9.4 million and paid net additions of 7.6 million, increases of 13% and 15%, respectively, from the same period last year.
The company’s fourth-quarter original-content roster includes the final season of “House of Cards” and the debut of “The Chilling Adventures of Sabrina,” based on the Archie Comics character Sabrina the Teenage Witch. Netflix plans to continue its aggressive spending on original content, estimating that free cash flow will be around negative-$3 billion for 2018.
Some analysts have voiced concern about Netflix’s use of debt to finance its free cash flow deficits. But the streaming giant is “approaching where the growth in operating profit is going to grow faster than our growth in content cash spend,” said Netflix Chief Financial Officer David Wells during the company’s earnings interview , adding that the company expects “material improvements in ’20.”
For now, most investors don’t seem to mind the negative free cash flow as long as subscriber numbers continue to grow.
During the company’s earnings call, executives also gave some clues about their strategy for India, which Chief Executive Reed Hastings said in February would be the source of the company’s “next 100 million subscribers.”
“We’ll go from expanding beyond English into Hindi and then into many more languages, more pricing options, more bundling — all of those things are possible,” Hastings said Tuesday.
“We’ll take it a million at a time and figure out how to expand the market as we grow,” he said.
In a letter to shareholders, Netflix acknowledged the rise of content competitors like AT&T Inc.’s T, +0.09% WarnerMedia and The Walt Disney Co. DIS, +2.42% as well as tech companies like Apple Inc. AAPL, +2.20% and Amazon.com, Inc AMZN, +3.35% .
“Amid these massive competitors on both sides, plus traditional media firms, our job is to make Netflix stand out so that when consumers have free time, they choose to spend it with our service,” the company wrote.
Netflix stock was still feeling the effects of the post-earnings decline last quarter, having fallen 13.5% in the past three months. The S&P 500 index SPX, +2.15% gained 0.4% in that period.
Sarah Toy Sarah Toy reports on the media for MarketWatch. She is based in New York.
